text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "All the countries of the world, all of them: there is not a single one that doesn't have as its goal to seek energy sovereignty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Asked about the principles that guide the energy sector after the reform, Sheinbaum listed five. They are energy sovereignty ("that we produce the energy we consume"), sustainability, social justice, national development, and a strong CFE as "a public company of the people of Mexico." Gasoline imports have fallen sharply since 2018, thanks to the Dos Bocas refinery, the Tula and Salina Cruz cokers, and the purchase of the Deer Park refinery. The biggest dependence left is gas: 75% of the natural gas Mexico consumes comes from the United States. That is why solar, wind and geothermal power are being expanded.

🚨🇲🇽 "When I know there is interference, I say it, no problem... And there is a basic principle: respect for our sovereignty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 El Universal asked about López Obrador's new book. It says US agencies fabricated cases against Sinaloa governor Rubén Rocha and senator Enrique Inzunza, and it calls the capture of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada an extrajudicial, interventionist US action. Sheinbaum said she has called many US actions interventionist, including before the people at the Monument to the Revolution. She pointed to files declassified by the agencies themselves, among them recently published documents on a US agency's interference around the 1968 student movement. She also noted that much of the family of one of El Chapo's sons was received at the US border: "a fact, not an interpretation."

🇲🇽🛢️ "A week ago there was a critical situation in the United States. They warned they would stop sending around a fifth of the imported natural gas we take into the national pipelines. It was a heavy blow." — Cuitláhuac García, director of Cenagas, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 75% of the natural gas Mexico consumes comes from the United States, and gas fuels 60–62% of its power generation. Mexico has no gas storage. By coordinating Pemex, CFE and the grid operator, and drawing on the gas held in its 21,000 km of pipelines, it could hold out for up to three days if imports were cut. Sheinbaum said the answer is more solar, wind and geothermal power, recovering the gas now flared, and studying unconventional gas in Coahuila only if it does not compete for water.
banner: 75% OF MEXICO'S GAS COMES FROM THE US

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "I think nepotism does a lot of damage to the country." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 A reporter asked about PAN mayors in Huixquilucan, Metepec and Atizapán seeking to be succeeded by their spouses. From 2030, the Constitution bars any relative up to the fourth degree from succeeding someone in an elected office, and re-election ends. Morena has already ruled it out for its own candidates in 2027. "In '30, that's over." Sheinbaum said the old Supreme Court was the branch with the most nepotism of all, and that the judiciary will be free of it after the 2028 judicial election.

🇲🇽🏭 "It is a historic investment, for around 38,000 megawatts." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Over the six-year term, 1.168 trillion pesos go to electricity and gas pipelines. Generation gets 794 billion: about 200 billion private, 452 billion in mixed projects that pass to CFE, and 142 billion from CFE directly. Transmission gets 161 billion, distribution 72 billion, and gas pipelines 140.9 billion. Six new combined-cycle plants have opened in two years, adding 3,203 MW. 55 solar and wind plants are under construction, and Puerto Peñasco will become one of the five largest solar plants in the world, at 1,000 MW.

🇲🇽⚖️ "From 2028, whoever wants to run for governor, head of government, or President of the Republic can only be Mexican." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Sheinbaum signed the decree for the constitutional reform, which passed with two-thirds of both chambers of Congress and 22 state legislatures. It was published today in the official gazette. Candidates for President, governor or Mexico City head of government who hold another nationality must renounce it before registering with the electoral institute. Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde said regulations will set out the procedure, including with the other country. The government's weekly "lie detector" rejected claims that the reform strips political rights: anyone with dual nationality can still run once they renounce it.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>The US Cut a Fifth of Mexico's Gas Imports. The Country Had Three Days of Reserves.</u>

Cuitláhuac García, director of Mexico's National Gas Control Center (Cenagas), revealed that a week ago the United States warned it would stop sending "about a fifth of the imported natural gas" that flows through Mexico's pipelines. If imports from the US were cut entirely, Mexico would have gas for only three days, because the country has almost no storage. About 75% of the gas Mexico burns comes from the US, and it generates around 60% of the country's electricity. Neoliberal governments dismantled national production and never built storage, leaving that dependence in place. (El Financiero)
banner: US CUTS 20% OF GAS: 3 DAYS OF RESERVES

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN Ex-Deputy Sentenced for 65 Million Peso Fraud, and Maru Campos's Government Kept Paying Him</u>

A court in Tlalnepantla sentenced Ismael Mario Rodríguez Saldaña, a former PAN state deputy in Chihuahua and a construction businessman, to two years in prison and ordered him to repay 65 million pesos for defrauding the developer Roagmex. Companies tied to him and his family had received at least four public-works contracts worth 196.27 million pesos from the Chihuahua Ministry of Communications and Public Works under PAN Governor Maru Campos. This is the same governor who lectures the federal government about the rule of law.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>After Newborn Deaths in Jalisco, IMSS Opens an Independent Audit and Inspects All 77 Neonatal ICUs</u>

Mexico's IMSS has opened an independent clinical audit into infections and deaths in the neonatal ICU of the National Medical Center in Jalisco, its second largest. A panel of neonatologists, infectious disease specialists and epidemiologists will review every file, and IMSS cannot change their conclusions. The national epidemiology lab, InDRE, will trace every microorganism found. Health authorities are also inspecting all 77 IMSS neonatal ICUs and their 660 cribs nationwide, checking hand-washing, catheter care, antibiotic use, water and staffing. IMSS director Zoé Robledo said the goal is to find failures and prevent new cases, not to criminalize medical staff.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A Supreme Court Justice Wrote a Ruling for a Coca-Cola Bottler, Then Pulled It</u>

Before today's Supreme Court debate on banning junk food in Mexican schools, Justice Giovanni Figueroa Mejía circulated a draft that would have granted an amparo to Embotelladora Las Margaritas (Grupo Rica), which bottles Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Del Valle and Powerade. The draft let it sell its products in universities again, arguing that "the elimination of foods that do not favor students' health" applies "only to schools that provide basic education." Contralínea obtained that first version. Figueroa swapped it for a draft that upholds the SEP ban before the vote. The original stayed on record.
banner: JUNK FOOD: JUSTICE'S COKE DRAFT PULLED
